name: Intracardiac neuron (intrinsic nervous system)
short_description: Multipolar ganglion neuron of the heart's own nerve network, sitting in a small ganglion of the epicardial ganglionated plexus and wrapped in satellite glia: it senses the heart's stretch and chemistry and trims rate and force locally, before the brain can react.

textbook.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; muted, slightly desaturated educational palette with thin clean outlines on a neutral dark-charcoal background, no border or frame and no baked-in text. Correct peripheral-ganglion morphology: one plump round-oval soma with a compact bushy dendritic arbour and exactly one fine axon leaving to the right — not a pyramidal cell, not a long myelinated tract. Quarter cut-away opened in the cell's own wall (no detached inset panel) shows ONE pale-lilac vesicular nucleus with a single deep-violet nucleolus and coarse slate-blue Nissl clumps. The satellite glial sheath is present and unmistakable — a continuous sage-green envelope carrying flattened glial nuclei, wrapping the soma and lifted open over the cut-away — and the ganglion context is all there: a grey-lavender connective-tissue capsule, a neighbouring ensheathed soma behind on the left, an ivory interganglionic nerve trunk entering and leaving, ochre epicardial fat cells crowding the outside and a terracotta band of atrial myocardium beneath. Dusty-blue preganglionic boutons sit on the soma. Clearly reads as a neuron inside a ganglion inside the heart wall, not as the generic isolated neuron plate)

sem.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; false-colour surface-only micrograph, correct for the modality — no internal organelles, no nucleus, no cut-away. A plump amber ganglion-neuron soma with short thick tapering dendrites and one finer axon, largely covered by a smooth draped teal SATELLITE GLIAL SHEATH whose overlapping flattened cell margins and nuclear bulges are readable, torn open over one flank to expose the neuron's own microvillous membrane with small rounded synaptic boutons on it. Behind it, further ensheathed somata, a bundle of fine parallel nerve fibres and a bed of wavy collagen fibrils; shallow depth of field, cool lighting, dark charcoal background. No myelin internodes, no Nodes of Ranvier, no motor end-plate, no striated muscle, no text, no scale bar, no border)

3d.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; natural, clearly distinguishable biological tints — warm rose-cream soma, pale-lilac nucleus with a deep-violet nucleolus, slate-blue Nissl clumps, pale-sage translucent satellite glial sheath with its own small green nuclei, dusty-blue preganglionic boutons, ivory nerve bundle, ochre fat, terracotta myocardium — neither near-monochrome nor neon. Soft global illumination, subsurface scattering, clean seamless dark studio background, no border. The whole small ganglion is shown enclosed in a translucent grey-lavender capsule with two further ensheathed neurons behind the main cell and the axon running out into the interganglionic nerve, which is exactly the 'neuron inside a ganglion in the heart wall' reading the reference asks for. Single main specimen, one nucleus, one nucleolus, no myelin, no end-plate, no text)

watercolor.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; warm aged paper fills the whole frame corner to corner with a soft darker wash halo painted directly onto it — no mat, frame, drop shadow or sheet-on-a-surface — subject large and centred, translucent washes over fine ink linework. Correct compact multipolar ganglion cell with a painterly cut-away showing one pale-lilac nucleus, a single deep-violet nucleolus and soft slate-blue Nissl stipple; the sage-green satellite glial cells are drawn individually around the soma, and the ganglion capsule, a faint neighbouring soma, the straw-ochre interganglionic nerve, ochre epicardial fat cells and a terracotta band of atrial muscle give the heart-wall context. No myelin internodes, no motor end-plate, no pyramidal cell, no text, no border)

reference: pass as an autonomic-ganglion plate, with an explicit caveat (Wikimedia Commons "Parasympathetic Ganglion (3595785930).jpg", CC BY 2.0, Ed Uthman; a genuine high-magnification H&E light micrograph of a parasympathetic autonomic ganglion, viewed before use: large plump ganglion-neuron somata with big pale vesicular nuclei each carrying one prominent dark nucleolus, granular Nissl-rich cytoplasm, and rings of small dark flattened satellite-glial nuclei hugging every soma, embedded in connective tissue with nerve fibre bundles between. Caveat stated plainly in §2 and repeated here: this is NOT specifically a cardiac ganglion — it is a parasympathetic ganglion from an extracardiac site. No freely-licensed high-magnification micrograph of a human intracardiac ganglion exists on Wikimedia Commons, and the open-access alternatives found were either low-magnification overviews where ganglia are only purple blobs or small grainy DIC panels with baked-in scale bars. The architecture is the correct one — an intracardiac ganglion is an autonomic ganglion and looks like this, differing mainly in its setting in an epicardial fat pad. No brain or spinal-cord neuron was substituted. Cleaned with edit_image.py: text/border removal, gentle recompose onto the somata, H&E colorization kept, no invented structures)
